subject: RFI: validation cadence and credit-model assumptions for SLA measurement
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@stellarus.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellarus.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RFI follow-up: how Redwood measures uptime and calculates credits (details requested)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the product overview last week. The procurement team has a couple of detailed follow-ups for our SRE and compliance reviewers before we include Redwood in the finalist list. Can you confirm the following items so we can validate against our procurement scoring?

1) How do you define "system availability" for multi-region clusters (per-region vs global)? Do you measure per-route or only at the model-inference endpoint level?

2) What synthetic probe cadence do you use to measure latency and availability in a region? Are probes synthetic-only or do you combine synthetic and real-traffic sampling?

3) How do you attribute partial degradations (e.g., 30% elevated latency for 2 hours) when computing service credits? Is there a continuous-weighting formula?

4) We need a sample evidence package (metrified CSVs, sample probe responses) and your recommended client-side instrumentation guidance (sampling rates, headers, correlation ids). Is that something you can attach?

Could you provide a short, shareable write-up for our auditors and attach any sample config/attachments? We aim to close the RFP thread by end of next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Senior Sourcing Manager, Stellarus Financial

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: how Redwood measures uptime and calculates credits (details requested)

Alicia — thanks for the clear list. I’ve drafted answers below and attached a concise evidence bundle and a probe config sample. Karthik (serving/runtime) and Monica (solutions) are cc’d for any technical follow-ups.

Summary answers (short):
- Availability model: Redwood reports availability both per-region and as a weighted global view. Service credit triggers are computed per-managed-customer endpoint (i.e., the path you call) and then aggregated to the monthly invoice.
- Probe cadence: default synthetic probes are 1/min/region (can be tightened to 15s for dedicated customers). We combine synthetic probes with probabilistic real-traffic sampling (1–5% by default) to catch client-side latency regressions.
- Partial degradations: we use a time-weighted crediting formula that converts latency buckets into an "equivalent outage" duration; credits are proportional to the aggregated equivalent outage within the monthly window.
- Evidence & telemetry: attached PDF includes sample CSVs and recommended trace headers (x-redwood-trace-id, x-client-request-ts). The probe YAML shows region/cadence examples.

I’ll expand the short answers below with exact formulas and a worked example for the RFP. If you want the dedicated cadence/penalty language (customer-specific), we can also include optional SLA addenda.

Best,
Rafael
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — that helps. A couple of clarifications from our SRE:

- For the time-weighted formula, can you provide the exact bucket thresholds you use for latency (e.g., p95 > 250ms = x multiplier)? Our scoring model needs deterministic thresholds.
- Are synthetic probes performed from public Internet vantage points or from private peering (we run a mix of direct peered traffic)?
- For redaction/compliance, which fields in the sample CSVs are PII? We need to make sure the evidence we store in our audit binder doesn't contain customer data.

If you can respond by tomorrow EOD we can slot this into our scoring matrix.

— Alicia

From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@stellarus.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI follow-up: how Redwood measures uptime and calculates credits (details requested)

Alicia — appreciate the follow-ups. Full responses below; I’ve also attached a short PDF (Redwood_SLA_Metering_Method_v1.pdf) and a probe-config-samples.yaml file in case your SRE wants to test locally. There’s also a Drive folder with anonymized CSVs.

1) Deterministic latency buckets (how we map to equivalent outage) — these are the defaults we use in our hosted SLA; customers can opt to adjust thresholds in Dedicated contracts: 
- Bucket A: p99 <= 750ms -> multiplier 0.0 (no outage)
- Bucket B: p99 in (750ms, 1500ms] -> multiplier 0.25
- Bucket C: p99 in (1500ms, 5000ms] -> multiplier 0.75
- Bucket D: p99 > 5000ms OR error rate > 5% -> multiplier 1.0 (equivalent full outage)

Computation: for each 1-minute window we compute the p99; map to a multiplier m; the equivalent outage seconds for that minute = m * 60. Sum across the monthly window to get total equivalent outage seconds. Service credit percentage is then credit = min(30, floor((equivalent_outage_seconds / total_month_seconds) * 100 * scaling_factor)) where scaling_factor is 1.0 for hosted accounts and 1.5 for multi-tenant burst scenarios. The attached PDF includes a worked example with numbers.

2) Probe vantage points — default synthetic probes are executed from a mix of public cloud vantage points in each target region (AWS/GCP/Azure public probes) plus our optional private-peering probes for Dedicated customers that opt-in. For Stellarus we can enable probes over your peering if you provide IP ranges.

3) PII redaction in evidence CSVs — our sample CSVs contain only anonymized request ids, timestamps, latency_ms, status_code, region, and probe_vantage. We redact any user payloads and strip headers that may contain PII. Fields considered PII (and excluded): authorization headers, user_email, user_id. We include trace IDs only.

Operational notes and recommendations:
- Recommended synthetic cadence for financial workloads: 1 probe/30s per region, combine with 2% real-traffic sampling of production traces for cross-checking.
- For legal clarity we provide a monthly credit summary and raw monthly windows on request; the monthly invoice shows the computed credit and the supporting evidence link.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Metering_Method_v1.pdf (worked example + formulas), probe-config-samples.yaml (probe targets, headers, frequency).
